description: This course covers numerical methods for solving mathematical problems in engineering and computer science. Topics include numerical solutions for linear and nonlinear equations using Newton-Raphson and bisection methods; interpolation techniques such as Lagrange and Newton divided difference polynomials; numerical integration methods like Simpson's rule and trapezoidal rule; numerical differentiation using finite differences; numerical solutions for systems of linear equations using Gaussian elimination and LU decomposition; matrix operations and eigenvalues; numerical methods for ordinary differential equations such as Euler's method, Runge-Kutta methods, and multistep methods; and error analysis using floating-point arithmetic and condition numbers. The course also covers the IEEE 754 standard for floating-point computation and the use of MATLAB for implementing numerical algorithms.

clos.text: Define the concepts of numerical analysis and explain the importance of numerical methods in solving engineering and scientific problems.
Describe the principles of numerical integration and differentiation, and implement these methods using MATLAB.
Explain the convergence criteria for iterative methods and apply them to solve nonlinear equations.
Implement numerical algorithms for solving systems of linear equations using Gaussian elimination and LU decomposition.
Evaluate the accuracy and stability of numerical methods using error analysis and IEEE 754 floating-point arithmetic.
